name: Being Wronged
overview: Scripture teaches that when believers are wronged, they are called to respond with patience and trust in the Lord rather than seeking personal revenge, as Proverbs 20:22 encourages waiting on God for deliverance. Jesus affirms this attitude by instructing us to treat others as we would want to be treated (Matthew 7:12) and to seek reconciliation privately when offenses occur (Matthew 18:15). Though the world brings tribulation, believers can have peace because Christ has overcome the world (John 16:33), and those who wait on the Lord will ultimately inherit the earth while evildoers face judgment (Psalms 37:9). This perspective centers on mercy, judgment, and the assurance of God's justice (Psalms 101:1).
